resources.string: Automatically tap Skip when it becomes available in the official YouTube app.
Auto Skip needs accessibility access to read YouTube’s on-screen controls and tap its Skip button for you. Processing stays on your device. The app does not save or transmit screen content.
1. Open Accessibility Settings below.\n2. Find Auto Skip under installed or downloaded apps.\n3. Enable the service, then return here.
Auto-skip is on. Tap to pause.
Auto Skip will not tap anything. Tap the power button to turn it on.
Tap the power button to enable access.
Ads without a Skip button will play normally. YouTube updates can change button detection.

Accessibility access
Open Accessibility Settings, select Auto Skip and enable it. Android may place it under Downloaded apps or Installed apps.

Restricted settings
For a downloaded APK, Android may block this setting. If you trust this build, open App info → the menu → Allow restricted settings, if available, then try accessibility setup again. The exact steps vary by phone.

Still not skipping?
Check that Auto-skip is on, accessibility access is enabled, and you’re using the official YouTube phone/tablet app. Some phones may stop accessibility services; check your manufacturer’s background-app settings if access stops working.

Only recognized, available Skip buttons are clicked. If YouTube changes its interface, an app update may be needed. Android TV is not supported in this version.
Settings could not be opened. Open your phone’s Settings app and find Accessibility → Auto Skip.

Automatically presses recognized, available Skip buttons in the official YouTube app. Requires reading YouTube’s interface and performing clicks. No screen content is stored or sent. You can pause in Auto Skip or disable this service here.
On the next screen, select Auto Skip and enable the service. Then return here.
